# clang-tidy Conventions — openSeaChest

## Overview

Static analysis runs via **clang-tidy** using the `.clang-tidy` file at the repository root (identical copies in each subproject). The configuration uses `FormatStyle: 'file'` so it also respects `.clang-format`.

Reference: [clang.llvm.org/extra/clang-tidy](https://clang.llvm.org/extra/clang-tidy/)

## Enabled Check Groups

All checks start disabled (`-*`), then these groups are explicitly enabled:

| Group | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `modernize-*` | C++ modernization patterns (with exceptions — see below) |
| `cert-*` | SEI CERT C/C++ Secure Coding Standard |
| `bugprone-*` | Common bug-prone patterns (with exceptions — see below) |
| `clang-analyzer-*` | Deep static analysis (with exceptions — see below) |
| `misc-*` | Miscellaneous checks (with exceptions — see below) |

Plus these individual `readability-*` checks (the full group is too noisy; only these are active):

- `readability-non-const-parameter` — add `const` to parameters that are not modified
- `readability-inconsistent-declaration-parameter-name` — parameter names must match between declaration and definition
- `readability-redundant-control-flow` — remove redundant `return`/`continue` at end of scope
- `readability-duplicate-include` — flag duplicate `#include` directives
- `readability-avoid-const-params-in-decls` — don't use `const` on value parameters in declarations (only definitions)
- `readability-function-cognitive-complexity` — enforce cognitive complexity limit (see below)

## Cognitive Complexity

```yaml
CheckOptions:
  - key: readability-function-cognitive-complexity.Threshold
    value: 100
```

The threshold is set to **100** as a pragmatic starting point — the default is 25. The goal is to **reduce complexity over time back toward 25**. When writing new code or refactoring:

- Target cognitive complexity ≤ 25 for new functions.
- Do not make existing high-complexity functions worse.
- Use the `refactor-method-complexity-reduce` skill to help break down functions that exceed the threshold.

Cognitive complexity is distinct from cyclomatic complexity — it penalises nested control flow more heavily. Each level of nesting multiplies the cost.

## Disabled Checks and Rationale

These checks are explicitly suppressed. Do NOT re-enable them without addressing the root cause:

| Disabled Check | Reason |
|----------------|--------|
| `bugprone-easily-swappable-parameters` | Extremely noisy; many hits on intentional C11 Annex K–style API signatures where parameter order is intentional. |
| `bugprone-assignment-in-if-condition` | Disabled — the project has legitimate uses of assignment-in-condition. |
| `clang-analyzer-deadcode.DeadStores` | Many existing warnings; cleanup is a future task, not a blocker. |
| `misc-no-recursion` | Recursion is used intentionally in this codebase. |
| `misc-unused-parameters` | Too many false positives (platform-specific code leaves params unused on some paths). |
| `misc-include-cleaner` | The project wraps system headers for portability; this check produces excessive noise. |
| `modernize-macro-to-enum` | Requires C11 anonymous enums; the project still supports pre-C11 compilers. Re-enable when C11 is the minimum. |

## Header Filtering

```yaml
HeaderFilterRegex: '.*'
```

All headers are analysed — not just project headers. This catches issues in included code paths.

## Warnings as Errors

```yaml
WarningsAsErrors: ''
```

No checks are promoted to errors by default in the config file. CI may override this with `--warnings-as-errors=*` for gating.

## Running clang-tidy

```bash
# Single file
clang-tidy src/myfile.c -- -Iinclude -Isubprojects/opensea-common/include

# With compile_commands.json (preferred — generated by Meson)
clang-tidy -p builddir src/myfile.c

# All files via compile_commands.json
run-clang-tidy -p builddir

# Fix automatically where possible
run-clang-tidy -p builddir -fix
```

Meson generates `compile_commands.json` in the build directory — always use `-p <builddir>` for accurate results.

## Writing New Code

When writing new functions, ensure they:
1. Have no `bugprone-*` or `cert-*` violations.
2. Keep cognitive complexity ≤ 25.
3. Use `const` on all pointer/reference parameters that are not modified (`readability-non-const-parameter`).
4. Match parameter names exactly between `.h` declaration and `.c` definition (`readability-inconsistent-declaration-parameter-name`).
5. Have no duplicate `#include` directives.

When clang-tidy flags a violation, fix the code — do not add `// NOLINT` suppressions unless the check is a confirmed false positive on a specific line, and always include a comment explaining why.
